title: SR-0.04 Receipts match signatures, and what is claimed is in the tree
request: Asked for by the owner on 6 Nov 2026, on the outside seed analysis of that date, in his words: 'make a contract to solve all of this, you sign, its gets done'. The analysis found 146 signed bodies and 1 receipt, signed contracts whose named tests are not in the tree, builds parked after signing, pages that disagree with each other, and review by seats on one machine that the records call independent. This contract makes receipts match signatures and makes what is claimed be in the tree. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.35 (T3 is built after it lands, since both change the vault and log paths; SR-1.35 lands first, and this contract's base at signing is that commit or a later one, so that it is not inside this contract's range). It was reviewed against memev main d597366052ac48d890fea92ce41f0f1e98f6a328, where SR-0.04 is a free id. Review: review of this contract is by the second seat on the same machine and is not independent. Both seats are AI on one machine. T7 makes the records honest about that; only a human second reviewer (O2) changes it. Decisions carried, stated as decisions. (1) The owner holds signing authority, in his words of 6 Nov 2026: 'I should hold authority over signing and I can sign everything that needs to be signed'. (2) The freeze's review date is 13 Nov 2026; that date is the lead's proposal and the owner may change it. (3) T2e runs on GitHub-hosted runners, split into jobs under the 6-hour limit (the owner, by dialog with the lead, 6 Nov 2026, once the count was known: 1,381 commands, 814 of them red-green, 93 full-suite runs across 73 contracts). It never runs on the owner's Mac, where full suites have wedged the machine, and a throwaway runner cannot reach his files. (4) The owner approves T2d's command file by signing its hash. (5) He makes his own signing key under a passphrase only he knows (same dialog; T9). Rule 0, the freeze. From signing, no contract is drafted, signed or superseded in memev, memev-ops or memev-app, and no design record, tier or repository is added. After the freeze too, a stale index row or an unlisted scope path never causes a new signed version. Allowed: this contract; security fixes, through T4; SR-1.35, which is signed after the second seat's round and gets a receipt like any other; SR-3.02 (the merge conformance corpus) if the owner says so under O5. Fix pull requests in memev wait until T2 is closed, because each would land inside this contract's base..HEAD and fail its scope criteria; other repositories are unaffected. Exit: the freeze lifts when T2 is closed. If T2 is not closed by 13 Nov 2026, the owner decides whether it continues. The freeze holds the first trial's contracts (installers, PL-1, MU-1, BO-1) until then. What was checked of the analysis on 6 Nov, by running it. By the lead, true: 146 signed bodies and 1 receipt; 8 of 146 record a base commit; test/oplog-lock.test.mjs, test/oplog-lock-cli.test.mjs and test/nonce-persist.test.mjs do not exist; VaultLocked and MAX_BUCKETS are nowhere in src; the OAuth issuer is built from the Host header (src/server/http.mjs:141); the builds of SR-1.01, SR-1.06 and the trial stack sit in memev-ops under refs/parked/2026-11-05/; the live site says 'merged automatically' 3 times, 'free Business trial' 2 times and 'Coming Soon' 4 times; no release, no npm package, 0 stars; docs/tiers/free.md:74 headlines 'Edit on two machines at once, nothing to resolve'. By the second seat: 114 live bodies (SO 74, PG 35, SR 26, QL 10, other 1 before supersedes), 107 with no base, 145 of 146 with a null workdir, 143 with command criteria, 110 of 110 records holding the word 'independent'. Not checked by either seat: line counts and ratios, the analysis's own test run, the tagline count, the zip finding. Tasks: T1 numbers and a ratchet; T2 receipts for every live contract, in five parts that carry their own task ids so that other tasks can depend on one part (T2a a derived base, T2b the base is never chosen by hand, T2c where it runs, T2d the commands, T2e the runs and the receipts); T3 unpark and land; T4 security, nine items; T5 one truth; T6 the suite runs anywhere; T7 review says what it is, from now on; T8 the weekly file; T9 the owner's own signing key. Deliberately out, so silence is not read as missed: SR-1.09 (line lengths, cross-layer imports, duplicated helpers), SR-2.01 (embedding recall; first after the freeze, since memory recall ranks high in demand), and memev-cloud's placeholder licence. The owner's alone, with his answers of 6 Nov 2026 where he has given one. O1 Deploy the site: his go given; the honest labels are being deployed. O2 A human second reviewer: not now, his decision. O3 Legal: no lawyer, his decision kept; the seller is the licensor ('its me'). O4 Legal entity (SR-9.01): open. O5 Engine: on record, no merge engine is built in Memev, and the analysis's small Node merge is declined; the conformance corpus, SR-3.02, is built now if he says so. O6 One release: a tag, an npm package and an install address conflict with decisions on record, which are SR-1.20, D-01, the private trial and the hold on new releases; his choice. O7 Where T2 runs: answered, GitHub-hosted runners; review on 13 Nov 2026; he approves the command file. O8 Users: nothing here creates demand. O9 The TypeScript and Rust editions PG-03.4 and PG-03.5: stopped, his decision; their receipts say so. O10 Business trial: none for now, his decision. O11 memev-ops stays private, his decision: T2c's table says which contracts cannot be checked from outside. O12 The 28 signed preambles that the 5 Nov decision reads differently and does not re-sign: is a note in T7's register enough? Open. scripts/metrics/assurance.mjs prints two gated numbers: receipts over live signed contracts, and PASS receipts over live. With --json it prints one JSON object holding live, with_receipt, pass, live_without_receipt, receipts_not_pass_or_fail and fail_without_decision as whole numbers, and it names the contracts behind each

a PASS with its scope not judged (T2a: a derived base cannot judge scope) is counted apart: --json holds pass and pass_scope_not_judged, the printout names them separately, and nothing adds one to the other. Both are ratcheted and may not fall
a contract recorded NOT RUN (T2c) is counted apart as not_run, with its reason, is never a receipt, and stays in live_without_receipt until the owner has decided it

it also prints, as information only and not gates, each labelled 'information only, not a gate': gaps found by our gates over gaps found outside (read from a hand-kept ledger, scripts/metrics/outside-gaps.json), and lines of contract and document text per line of src in 7 days. Neither changes the exit code of any mode

live means every signed body in contracts/signed not named by another signed body's supersedes, in every area (SO, PG, SR, QL and any other). A body is left out of the live count only when a signed successor in the tree names it; a body marked superseded any other way (a manifest status, a README row) is still live, and --check names it

a receipt counts only if it holds the contract's hash and the commit it was run at, and both match: the hash equals the canonical hash of the signed body (canonicalHash of vendor/attest/signature.mjs), and the commit is a full 40-hex sha of a commit that exists in the checkout the receipt names. DRAFT 3 says only that both match; what the commit must match is fixed here and is open to the red-team round. The one receipt on main today (k-memory-quality-multiling-4468b8) holds neither, so it does not count until that contract is run again
verify writes both: each receipt entry that contractVerify appends (src/engine/contracts.mjs) carries a line 'contract <sha256>' and a line 'commit <sha>' for the workdir's HEAD

two committed ratchets, in scripts/metrics/assurance-ratchet.json: live contracts with no receipt may not rise above max_live_without_receipt, and PASS over live may not fall below min_pass_over_live. 'node scripts/metrics/assurance.mjs --check' exits 1 and names the contracts when either is broken. It also exits 1 when the ratchet file at HEAD is looser than any earlier committed version of itself (the maximum only falls, the minimum only rises)
the suite runs the check over this repository: one subtest of test/assurance.test.mjs runs --check in the repository root and asserts exit 0, so npm test and CI fail when a ratchet breaks

each red-green criterion has its own subtest in test/assurance.test.mjs whose name starts with the criterion's label (the text before its first colon), and the criterion runs only that subtest. Each subtest's first assertion fails at the base on an assertion and never on a load error: a new module or script is imported inside the subtest or run as a child process, and a new file is checked by an assertion that it exists before it is read. No criterion command pipes through tail or head, and each prints the whole captured output (docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md, 'Commands that cut their output' and 'False reds in signed criteria')

tasks.title: A base without re-signing and without a new signature
requirements: for a locally signed body that records no base, verify derives it from git history (src/engine/contract-base.mjs, called from contractVerify) and the receipt says 'base derived' with the commit
no record file and no key: nothing is written under contracts/signed or contracts/keys, the body's bytes do not change, its signature still verifies, and the body still has no base field

with no checkout of the repository that holds the body, scope and red-green criteria are BLOCKED with that reason; a shallow clone is refused; a checkout that holds a different contract under that name is BLOCKED

a derived base can judge tests and files and cannot judge scope. tasks.title: Where it runs
requirements: T2 never runs in a live vault or a seat's home. The runner (scripts/receipts/run.mjs, new) makes a scratch home and a scratch config folder (MEMEV_CONFIG_DIR). The scratch vault's root is the contract's detached checkout: workdir is null on 145 of 146 bodies, so verify runs in the vault's own folder (contracts.mjs), and a vault beside the checkout would find no test files. contracts.redteam_root is that same folder. For a body whose work is in another repository, that repository's checkout, with the body copied in
it refuses to start, and runs nothing, when HOME is the invoking account's own home folder, when the config folder already holds a vault registry, or when the vault folder already holds a vault

a checkout of the right repository per contract comes from a committed table, contracts/receipts/repositories.json: one row per live signed body, naming the repository its work is in (91 of 114 live bodies name none in their request). A live body with no row stops the run before anything runs. Each contract runs in a detached checkout of its repository

a stated timeout and budget: the runner takes a timeout per contract and a budget for the whole run, and both are written in the run record. A contract that passes its timeout is recorded as that and the run goes on; when the budget is used up the run stops and lists the contracts not run

where it runs is the owner's decision: GitHub-hosted runners. contracts/receipts/run-place.json names the runner and the workflow, .github/workflows/receipts.yml. The runner refuses to run unless GITHUB_ACTIONS is true, RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT is github-hosted and the workflow is that one. Those can be set by hand, so they are a guard against accident; the proof is the public run log, whose run id goes in the run record

the runner runs only commands that are in the approved command file (T2d): with no approval record, with a record whose hash is not the file's, or for a contract that holds a command the file does not list, it runs nothing for that contract and says why
the runner lists the commands: --list-commands prints every command, metric and red-green command of every live signed body once, in a stable order, as the file T2d commits

the run record (contracts/receipts/RUN.json) says who approved the command file and who ran (by role, never by name), the account and machine, the timeout and budget, when the run started, and for each contract the verdict and the receipt's contract hash and commit

each red-green criterion has its own subtest in test/receipts-run.test.mjs whose name starts with the criterion's label (the text before its first colon), and the criterion runs only that subtest. Each subtest's first assertion fails at the base on an assertion and never on a load error: a new module or script is imported inside the subtest or run as a child process, and a new file is checked by an assertion that it exists before it is read. No criterion command pipes through tail or head, and each prints the whole captured output (docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md, 'Commands that cut their output' and 'False reds in signed criteria')

the jobs: --shard i/n runs one part, and the parts cover every live signed body exactly once. The workflow starts by hand only (workflow_dispatch, never on a pull request, so a fork cannot start it), has permissions contents: read, uses no secret, and each job has timeout-minutes of 350 or fewer, under GitHub's 6-hour limit. Each job sets HOME to a scratch folder before the runner starts. --collect gathers the jobs' artifacts into contracts/receipts/, refusing a receipt whose hash or commit does not match

each row of contracts/receipts/repositories.json says whether its repository is public. The memev workflow holds no secret, so it cannot check out a private repository: a private row (when this was written about 5 live bodies and 17 commands: memev-ops 3, converge 1, memev-site 1) is left out of its shards and listed as running in its own repository. There the same runner runs in a workflow in that repository, using that repository's own token, and its artifact is brought back by hand through --collect, which checks the hash and commit. memev-ops stays private (the owner, 6 Nov 2026), so these contracts cannot be checked from outside, and --check-table names them. If that repository's Actions cannot run (billing stopped once, on 27 Oct), the contract is NOT RUN with the reason: T1 counts it apart, never as a receipt, and it needs an owner decision like a FAIL

tasks.title: The commands
requirements: the commands of every live contract (143 signed bodies held command criteria when the second seat counted on 6 Nov) are listed once in one file, contracts/receipts/commands.json, written by the runner's --list-commands and committed

the owner approves that file by its hash before any runs: contracts/receipts/commands.approval.json holds the file's sha256, the time of the approval, who approved and who ran. Both are written by role (the owner; the lead or the second seat), never as a name, handle or address, which the leak scan refuses

the approval is the owner's signature: the record holds a signature over the file's sha256 by his own key (T9). A signature proves the key, and the key is under a passphrase only he knows, so it says he acted as far as anything here can. The roles and times remain statements
the file is approved before T4's approval rule lands, so the two do not collide (T4 depends on this task)
tasks.description: This task builds no code: the runner that lists the commands and refuses an unapproved one is T2c (T2c-c08, T2c-c09). Its phase is verify, so it carries no red-green criterion.

done when every live contract has a valid receipt (T1's rule) and every FAIL and every NOT RUN has an owner decision recorded: build it, or withdraw it, or for a NOT RUN, run it later. tasks.title: The owner's own signing key
requirements: the owner holds signing authority ('I should hold authority over signing'), so signing must be something a seat cannot do in his place by running a command. He makes an Ed25519 key under a passphrase only he knows, in his own Terminal. The public half goes under contracts/keys, and the private half stays encrypted. Both seats run under his account, so they can read the encrypted file: the passphrase, and the strength of its encryption, are what protect it

contract signing and the approvals of T2d and T2e accept a passphrase-protected PEM: 'memev contract sign <id> --key FILE' asks for the passphrase on the terminal only. There is no flag or environment variable for it, so with no terminal it refuses and writes nothing

a vault setting, contracts.signer_keys, lists the keys allowed to sign there. When it is set, any other key is refused, and so is an unencrypted one. When it is not set, signing works as today, because a person using Memev alone keeps the automatic local key: that is why an unencrypted key is not refused everywhere

this repository sets the rule through a committed list, contracts/keys/OWNER-SIGNERS.json. scripts/contracts/check-signers.mjs fails if a signed body added after the list's first commit is signed by a key not on it, if a key in REVIEWER_KEYS is on it, or if the list changed without a signature by a key already on it. The suite runs it

docs/CONTRACTS.md says how to make the key: /usr/local/bin/openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 | /usr/local/bin/openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -v2 aes-256-cbc -iter 600000 -out FILE, which writes no plaintext to disk. 'genpkey -aes-256-cbc' alone uses 2048 iterations, too few when the seats can read the file and guess offline. /usr/bin/openssl (LibreSSL) has no Ed25519 here. It says the limit plainly: a signature proves the key, not the person, and a passphrase typed where a seat can read it is no longer his alone. A seat that changed the program he types the passphrase into could save it: the fresh clone below reduces that and does not remove it. Only a key on another device, such as a hardware key, removes it, and that is his choice

SR-0.04 itself is signed before this task is built, so its one signature is made by the owner with a small script the lead gives him, which decrypts the key in memory, and which T9's signing replaces. He runs it from a fresh clone at a commit sha he is given, in his own Terminal window and never through a session, naming his expected key id; it refuses any other key, and prints the contract's id, title and hash before it asks. The same holds for every signature he makes. SR-0.04's body is then the first entry check-signers holds him to

each red-green criterion has its own subtest in test/owner-key.test.mjs whose name starts with the criterion's label (the text before its first colon), and the criterion runs only that subtest. Each subtest's first assertion fails at the base on an assertion and never on a load error: a new module or script is imported inside the subtest or run as a child process, and a new file is checked by an assertion first
